summary: The cardholder starts a cycle with no previous balance, makes purchases that push the account above the numeric credit limit, and reaches statement close while still over limit. The scenario is designed to show an over-limit condition at statement close while also including bound events for the modeled minimum-payment and grace-period obligations.
assumptions: The account begins a new billing cycle with no previous balance, so the purchase grace-period condition is satisfied unless otherwise displaced by later facts.

The issuer-approved credit limit is $1000, and purchases in this cycle are authorized and posted even though they ultimately cause the balance to exceed that limit; this lets the scenario test over-limit behavior at statement close.
No payments are made before statement close, so the New Balance at statement close equals the sum of posted purchases in the cycle.

Because this archetype focuses on over-limit status at statement close, the minimum payment obligation is included by reference through a later due-check event after the statement is issued rather than being the main outcome of the scenario.
The issuer's grace-period obligation is represented by the statement-close event because the cycle starts with no previous balance and no purchase interest is imposed before at least 25 days elapse.

Any actual over-limit fee assessment under clause 7 is not separately modeled in the required clause bindings because the user limited obligation bindings to clause-4-credit-limit, clause-5-minimum-payment-obligation, and clause-6-grace-period.
